clue.text: Horseman about to enter section of track and run

indicators.note: to enter means the short word for about goes inside the stretch of track

parts.note: a lane is a marked-off section of a running track
C is short for circa, Latin for about
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rider is told to cut into a lane of the racecourse and gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalry soldier armed with a lance, so a mounted fighter.

clue.text: Tree planted in Matabeleland

indicators.note: planted in means the tree is buried inside the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: Someone has put a tree in the ground in a region of Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Designer of, fashions more comfortable around the midriff?

indicators.note: around means the word for more comfortable is wrapped round the word for the midriff

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more comfortable
tum is a colloquial word for the stomach or midriff

explanation.surface: A fashion house makes clothes that sit more easily on the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray comma after 'of' is a printing mark on the page; the definition reads 'Designer of fashions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes and clothes, a designer of dress.

clue.text: Female recruited to recycle waste

indicators.note: recruited means the letter for female is taken into the word for recycling

parts.note: to reuse something is to recycle it

explanation.surface: A woman has been signed up to help with a recycling scheme for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is rubbish, discarded material.

clue.text: Hesitation to add to shade mostly found in colourful range

indicators.note: to add to means the hesitation sound is tacked on after the trimmed ghost
mostly means the word for a ghostly shade loses its last letter

parts.note: a shade is a ghost, a spectre
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A pause in speech joins a faded hue in a bright array.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a colour in this colourful clue, but it is a ghost: SPECTRE, cut to SPECTR by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spectrum is the band of colours light splits into, a range of hues.

clue.text: Observe the formalities and rise as soon as royal money is distributed

parts.note: to stand is to rise to one's feet
once can mean as soon as, as in once he arrives
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

indicators.note: is distributed means the letters for royal and money are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Guests get to their feet the moment the monarch's cash is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is distributed' rearranges R plus MONEY into REMONY.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on correct etiquette and formal behaviour.

clue.text: Severely condemn river transport of inferior quality

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a crate is slang for a decrepit old car or plane

explanation.surface: Someone rails against a river ferry that is a poor vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or curse bitterly.

clue.text: What makes a hobby gripping?

parts.note: a hobby is also a small falcon, and the question asks what part of that bird lets it grip its prey

explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' reads as a pastime that holds the attention; it is the falcon, which grips with its claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey, used to seize and hold.

clue.text: Where colours may be fixed in bananas?

definitions.meaning: a ship's or regiment's colours, its flag, are hoisted aloft on a mast
bananas is slang for crazy or mad

explanation.walkthrough: UP THE POLE is British slang for mad or mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags are run up a flagstaff, and the same phrase is slang for being crazy.

clue.text: Banter, by its nature, keeping one to standard

indicators.note: keeping means the Latin phrase holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself or intrinsically
I is the Roman numeral for one
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: Light teasing, by definition, has to measure up to some benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a measure of quality; it is a banner, FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, frivolous mockery or teasing talk.

clue.text: Reluctant to remove head of clergy

indicators.note: to remove head of means the first letter of the word for clergy is dropped

parts.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to depose the leader of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of clergy' looks like a bishop; the clergy is THE CLOTH, and its head, C, goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth (also loath) means unwilling or disinclined.

clue.text: Drove off regular beat in light of traffic hold-up

indicators.note: in means the beat goes inside the colour of the stop light

parts.note: red is the traffic light that stops cars
a pulse is a regular beat, as of the heart

explanation.surface: A driver's heart thumps while waiting at a red light in a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back.

clue.text: Atlas, perhaps, right for one who wanders

parts.note: the Atlas is a mountain range in North Africa

explanation.surface: A book of maps is suited to a traveller who roams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atlas' suggests a book of maps or the Titan; it is the North African mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a rover, someone who ranges over country.

clue.text: American Indian dance with single accompaniment

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single unit going along with the dance

explanation.surface: A Native American dances to music from one accompanist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona.

clue.text: Speculator taken in by maturer operator with experience

indicators.note: taken in by means the speculator sits inside the word for maturer

parts.note: older means more mature
a stag is a speculator who buys new shares to sell them quickly

explanation.surface: A gambler on the stock market is fooled by a more seasoned dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' reads as deceived, which suits a gambler outwitted by a veteran, but it is the container signal. A stag is London Stock Exchange slang for a quick-profit share buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long practised at something.

clue.text: Representative signs books, surrounded by people

indicators.note: surrounded by means the books sit inside the word for a people

parts.note: a nation is a people
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A delegate autographs volumes while a crowd presses round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representative' looks like a person and 'signs' a verb; together they are the noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A notation is a system of symbols that stand for something, as in musical notation.

clue.text: Nightwatchman usually at No. 10 perhaps

parts.note: in cricket a nightwatchman is a lower-order batsman sent in late in the day, and number ten is near the bottom of the batting order

explanation.walkthrough: A nightwatchman and No. 10 suggest a guard at Downing Street; in cricket, a NIGHTWATCHMAN protects better batsmen at the end of a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is one of the weak batsmen at the bottom of a cricket batting order.

clue.text: He doesn't appear overjoyed in a social gathering

indicators.note: in means the word for overjoyed is set within the other pieces

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work and company, as in a sewing bee
sent is slang for delighted or carried away

explanation.surface: A man who is thrilled at a party nevertheless keeps out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is one who is missing or fails to turn up.

clue.text: Fetching drink to be distributed around merry board

indicators.note: to be distributed around means the drink is split and set on either side of the other piece

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

indicators.note: merry means the letters of board are tipsily jumbled

explanation.surface: Attractive beer is to be handed out round a cheerful table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry' shuffles the board's letters, and 'to be distributed around' splits the drink so its first letter sits before them and its last two after. 'Fetching' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching here is the adjective meaning attractive or charming.

clue.text: Chills South with lead of diamonds

indicators.note: with lead of means the diamonds come first, ahead of the compass point

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: At the bridge table South feels cold after leading a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, South is a player and a lead is the first card; here 'lead of' puts ICE in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices as a verb means cools or freezes.

clue.text: Labels for tailors

definitions.meaning: names or titles by which people are called
to tailor is to cut or shape to suit, as a hairdresser shapes hair

explanation.definitionFit: A style is a title, and to style is to design or fashion something.

clue.text: Firm's initiation of special board meeting

indicators.note: initiation of means just the opening letter of special is used

parts.note: a table is a board, as in a board laid with food

explanation.surface: A company's board meeting opens with something special.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Firm's' stands for 'is'; 'board meeting' reads as a company session but 'meeting' just joins S to TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and secure, firmly fixed.

clue.text: Scholars in charge of foundation

parts.note: BAs are holders of a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Academics are in control of a college's founding.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means forming the base, fundamental.

clue.text: Earnest request to provide feed in field

indicators.note: in means the word for feed is put inside the word for field

parts.note: the entry is the field of competitors in a race
to eat is to feed

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to be allowed to graze cattle in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' looks like a meadow; it is the set of entrants, ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an urgent plea or appeal.

clue.text: It turns up on the tenth

indicators.note: turns up means the word it is written upwards in this down light

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something appears on the tenth day of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth part, historically of produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Spurs, for example, getting goals at both ends

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: at both ends means the first and last letters of goals are used

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, for one, scores at either end of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; here it is a verb, urges on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs, as in egging on, means urges or incites.

clue.text: Tumbledown lodge to try a hermit

indicators.note: tumbledown means the letters fall into disorder like a ruined building

explanation.surface: A recluse is invited to give a ramshackle cabin a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a cave dweller, by extension a recluse.

clue.text: Note garden feature in China

parts.note: C is a musical note
a rockery is a garden bed of stones and plants

explanation.surface: Someone notices a rock garden while travelling in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the start of a sentence hides its lower-case sense, porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain tableware, plates and cups.

clue.text: Credit secured by distinguished broadcast

indicators.note: secured by means credit is held inside the word for distinguished

parts.note: seen means made out, distinguished by sight

explanation.surface: A loan is guaranteed by an eminent television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to show it on television.
